sections.title: Types of Triangles

learn.title: Parts of a triangle
learn.html: The base is the side at the bottom. The vertex angle is the angle opposite the base. The 2 angles on the base are the base angles. The height is a line from the vertex that meets the base at a right angle (90°).

learn.title: Name the parts of triangle ABC
learn.html:
Base: BC
Vertex angle: ∠BAC
Base angles: ∠ABC and ∠BCA
Sides next to the vertex angle: BA and CA
Height: AD

learn.title: Equilateral triangle
learn.html:
An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides and 3 equal angles.

Each angle is 60°. The little tick marks show which sides are equal.

learn.title: Is this triangle equilateral?
learn.html:
All 3 sides are 3.5 cm. So AB = BC = AC.

Yes! It is an equilateral triangle, and every angle is 60°.

learn.title: Isosceles triangle
learn.html:
An isosceles triangle has 2 equal sides and 2 equal angles.

The 2 equal angles are opposite the 2 equal sides.

learn.title: Find the equal angles
learn.html:
PQ = PR = 3.5 cm. These are the 2 equal sides.

So the angles opposite them are equal: ∠PQR = ∠PRQ (the green arcs).

learn.title: Scalene triangle
learn.html: A scalene triangle has 3 different sides and 3 different angles.

learn.title: Is this triangle scalene?
learn.html:
The sides are 2 cm, 3 cm and 4 cm. No two sides are the same.

Yes! It is a scalene triangle.

learn.title: Right triangle
learn.html:
A right triangle has 1 right angle (90°). The small square shows the right angle.

The other 2 angles always add up to 90°.

learn.title: The other 2 angles
learn.html:
∠XYZ = 90°. ∠X = 35° and ∠Z = 55°.

35° + 55° = 90°. They add up to 90°, just like the rule says.

learn.title: Acute triangle
learn.html:
An acute angle is less than 90°.

In an acute triangle, all 3 angles are acute.

learn.title: Is this an acute triangle?
learn.html:
The angles are 60°, 70° and 50°. Each one is less than 90°.

Yes! It is an acute triangle.

learn.title: Obtuse triangle
learn.html:
An obtuse angle is more than 90° but less than 180°.

An obtuse triangle has 1 obtuse angle. An obtuse triangle can also be isosceles.

learn.title: Is this an obtuse triangle?
learn.html:
The angles are 120°, 30° and 30°. 120° is more than 90°.

Yes! It is an obtuse triangle. It also has 2 equal angles, so it is isosceles too.

learn.title: One triangle, two names
learn.html:
Look at the sides: equilateral, isosceles or scalene.

Look at the angles: acute, right or obtuse.

So one triangle can have two names. Every equilateral triangle is also acute (60°, 60°, 60°).

learn.title: A right isosceles triangle
learn.html:
Angles: 90°, 45° and 45°. It has a right angle, so it is a right triangle.

It has 2 equal angles, so it is also an isosceles triangle.

questions.label: Do and Learn 1 (a)
questions.q:
Fill in the blanks.
PQ = ___ = ___
∠p = ∠q = ∠___ = ___°
questions.hint: Look at the tick marks. How many sides are equal?
steps: Each side of the triangle has 1 tick mark. Same tick marks mean the sides are equal.
So all 3 sides are equal: PQ = PR = QR. This is an equilateral triangle.
An equilateral triangle has 3 equal angles. All the angles add up to 180°.
questions.why: All 3 sides have the same tick mark, so the triangle is equilateral, and each angle is 60°.

questions.label: Do and Learn 1 (b)
questions.q:
Fill in the blanks.
∠g = ∠___
EG = ___
questions.hint: Find the 2 sides with the same tick marks.
steps: EG and EF both have 2 tick marks. So EG = EF. This is an isosceles triangle.
In an isosceles triangle, the 2 angles opposite the equal sides are equal.
∠g is opposite side EF. ∠f is opposite side EG.
So ∠g = ∠f.
questions.why: The angles opposite the 2 equal sides of an isosceles triangle are equal.

questions.label: Do and Learn 1 (c)
questions.q:
Fill in the blanks.
∠v = ___°
∠u + ∠w = ___°
questions.hint: The small square means a right angle.
steps: ∠v has a small square. A small square means a right angle, so ∠v = 90°.
All 3 angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
questions.why: In a right triangle, the other 2 angles add up to 90°.

questions.label: Do and Learn 2 (a)
questions.q: Name the type of triangle.
questions.hint: Is any angle 90° or bigger?
steps: The angles are 47°, 53° and 80°.
47° is less than 90°. 53° is less than 90°. 80° is less than 90°.
All 3 angles are acute, so it is an acute triangle.
questions.why: All 3 angles are less than 90°.

questions.label: Do and Learn 2 (b)
questions.q: Name the type of triangle.
questions.hint: Is any angle bigger than 90°?
steps: The angles are 40°, 115° and 25°.
115° is more than 90° and less than 180°. So 115° is an obtuse angle.
A triangle with 1 obtuse angle is an obtuse triangle.
questions.why: ∠XYZ = 115° is an obtuse angle.

questions.label: Exercise 1 (a)
questions.q:
Fill in the blanks.
Given that CB is the base of triangle ABC.
Vertex angle: ___
Base angles: ___ and ___
Sides adjacent to vertex angle: ___ and ___
Height: ___
questions.hint: The vertex angle is at the corner that is NOT on the base.
steps: The base is CB. The corner not on the base is A. So the vertex angle is ∠CAB.
The base angles are the 2 angles on the base CB: ∠ACB and ∠CBA.
The sides that touch the vertex angle at A are CA and BA.
The height goes from A down to the base at a right angle. ∠ACB is already a right angle, so the height is AC.
questions.answer: Vertex angle: ∠CAB; Base angles: ∠ACB and ∠CBA; Sides: CA and BA; Height: AC
questions.why: AC meets the base CB at a right angle, so AC is the height.

questions.label: Exercise 1 (b)
questions.q:
Fill in the blanks.
Given that UT is the base of triangle STU.
Vertex angle: ___
Base angles: ___ and ___
Sides adjacent to vertex angle: ___ and ___
Height: ___
questions.hint: Find the corner that is not on UT.
steps: The base is UT. The corner not on the base is S. So the vertex angle is ∠UST.
The base angles are on the base UT: ∠SUT and ∠UTS.
The sides that touch the vertex angle at S are US and TS.
SV goes from S to the base and makes a right angle. So the height is SV.
questions.answer: Vertex angle: ∠UST; Base angles: ∠SUT and ∠UTS; Sides: US and TS; Height: SV
questions.why: SV is drawn from the vertex S and is perpendicular to the base UT.

questions.label: Exercise 1 (c)
questions.q:
Fill in the blanks.
Given that LK is the base of triangle IKL.
Vertex angle: ___
Base angles: ___ and ___
Sides adjacent to vertex angle: ___ and ___
Height: ___
questions.hint: The height can be outside the triangle. Look for the dotted line with a right angle.
steps: The base is LK. The corner not on the base is I. So the vertex angle is ∠LIK.
The base angles are on the base LK: ∠ILK and ∠LKI.
The sides that touch the vertex angle at I are LI and KI.
The base LK is made longer (dotted line) to J. IJ meets it at a right angle. So the height is IJ.
questions.answer: Vertex angle: ∠LIK; Base angles: ∠ILK and ∠LKI; Sides: LI and KI; Height: IJ
questions.why: For an obtuse triangle, the height can fall outside. IJ is perpendicular to the base line.

questions.label: Exercise 2
questions.q:
Group the triangles and write the letters in the table correctly.
Equilateral triangleIsosceles triangleRight triangle
???
questions.hint: Look for clues: tick marks (equal sides), equal lengths, 60° angles, and small squares (right angles).
steps: Equilateral (3 equal sides or three 60° angles): D has three 60° angles. F has a tick mark on all 3 sides. So D and F.
Isosceles (2 equal sides or 2 equal angles): B has 2 sides with tick marks. C has two sides of 15 cm. G has two angles of 30°. So B, C and G.
Right (a small square): A, E and H each have a small square. So A, E and H.
questions.answer: Equilateral: D, F · Isosceles: B, C, G · Right: A, E, H
questions.why: Tick marks and equal numbers show equal sides or angles. A small square shows a right angle.

questions.label: Exercise 3 (a)
questions.q:
Identify the triangles in the figure and write the letters in the table below.
Equilateral triangle?
Isosceles triangle?
Right triangle?
questions.hint: First find the triangles with a right angle (small square). Then look at the shape of each of the others.
steps: The small squares are in D and E. So the right triangles are D and E.
K has 3 sides that are the same length. So K is equilateral.
A, B, C, F, H and G each have 2 sides that are the same length. So the isosceles triangles are A, B, C, F, H and G.
questions.answer: Equilateral: K · Isosceles: A, B, C, F, H, G · Right: D, E
questions.why: Right triangles have a right angle, an equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides, and an isosceles triangle has 2 equal sides.

questions.label: Exercise 3 (b)
questions.q:
Identify the triangles in the figure and write the letters in the table below.
Acute triangle?
Obtuse triangle?
questions.hint: An obtuse triangle has one wide angle (more than 90°). D and E have right angles, so they go in neither row.
steps: D and E have a right angle, so they are not acute and not obtuse.
K is equilateral (60°, 60°, 60°). H has 3 small, sharp angles. So the acute triangles are K and H.
A, B, C, F and G each have one wide angle bigger than 90°. So the obtuse triangles are A, B, C, F and G.
questions.answer: Acute: K, H · Obtuse: A, B, C, F, G
questions.why: In an acute triangle all angles are less than 90°. An obtuse triangle has 1 angle more than 90°.

questions.label: Exercise 4 (a)
questions.q:
Put a tick (✓) in the box for each correct statement.
The square below is divided into halves.
There are:
• 2 equilateral triangles
• 2 isosceles triangles
• 2 right triangles
questions.hint: A square has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles.
steps: Each half has 2 sides of the square. The sides of a square are equal, so each half has 2 equal sides. ✓ isosceles.
Each half has 1 corner of the square. A square's corner is a right angle. ✓ right triangle.
The long side (the cut) is longer than the square's sides, so the 3 sides are not all equal. ✗ equilateral.
questions.answer: ✓ 2 isosceles triangles, ✓ 2 right triangles (✗ 2 equilateral triangles)
questions.why: Each half has 2 equal sides and a right angle, but not 3 equal sides.

questions.label: Exercise 4 (b)
questions.q:
Put a tick (✓) in the box for each correct statement.
The rectangle below is divided into halves.
Each half is:
• an equilateral triangle
• an isosceles triangle
• a right triangle
questions.hint: A rectangle has a long side and a short side.
steps: Each half has a corner of the rectangle. That corner is a right angle. ✓ right triangle.
Each half has a long side, a short side and the cut. All 3 are different lengths. ✗ isosceles.
The sides are not all equal. ✗ equilateral.
questions.why: The 3 sides of each half are all different, but each half has a right angle.

questions.label: Exercise 5 (a)
questions.q:
Answer the following question.
What type of triangle has 3 different sides?
questions.hint: Think: equilateral, isosceles or scalene?
steps: Equilateral has 3 equal sides. Isosceles has 2 equal sides.
A triangle with no equal sides (3 different sides) is a scalene triangle.
questions.why: A scalene triangle has 3 different sides and 3 different angles.

questions.label: Exercise 5 (b)
questions.q:
Answer the following question.
What type of triangle has 1 obtuse angle?
questions.hint: Think: acute, right or obtuse?
steps: An obtuse angle is more than 90° but less than 180°.
A triangle with 1 obtuse angle is an obtuse triangle.
questions.why: The name of the triangle comes from its biggest angle.

questions.label: Exercise 5 (c)
questions.q:
Answer the following question.
What type of triangle does not have only 1 acute angle or at least 1 obtuse angle?
questions.hint: If a triangle has no obtuse angle (and no right angle), what are all its angles?
steps: The triangle has no obtuse angle.
It also does not have just 1 acute angle. So it has more acute angles: in fact all 3 angles are acute.
A triangle with 3 acute angles is an acute triangle.
questions.why: All the angles in an acute triangle are acute angles.

learn.title: Angles of a triangle add up to 180°
learn.html:
Tear off the 3 corners of any paper triangle and put them side by side. They make a straight line.

A straight line is 180°. So the 3 angles of a triangle always add up to 180°.

learn.title: Try it with numbers
learn.html:
An equilateral triangle: 60° + 60° + 60° = 180° ✓

A right triangle with 90°, 30° and 60°: 90° + 30° + 60° = 180° ✓

learn.title: Finding a missing angle
learn.html:
Start with 180°. Take away the angles you know. What is left is the missing angle.

Missing angle = 180° - first angle - second angle

learn.title: Angles in an isosceles triangle
learn.html:
The 2 angles opposite the equal sides are equal.

To find one of them: (180° - the other angle) ÷ 2

learn.title: ABC is isosceles. Find ∠ACB.
learn.html:
∠ACB = ∠ABC (they are opposite the equal sides).

∠ACB + ∠ABC = 180° - 68° = 112°

∠ACB = 112° ÷ 2 = 56°

learn.title: Two more helpful facts
learn.html:
In a right triangle, the other 2 angles add up to 90°.

Angles on a straight line add up to 180°.

learn.title: Find ∠a and ∠b
learn.html:
EFH is a right triangle. EGH is isosceles with EH = GH and ∠EHG = 66°.

∠b = 180° - 90° - 66° = 24°

∠GEH = (180° - 66°) ÷ 2 = 114° ÷ 2 = 57°

∠a = 90° - 57° = 33°

learn.title: BCD is a straight line. Find ∠x.
learn.html:
∠DAC = 72°, ∠ADC = 48°.

In triangle ACD: ∠ACD = 180° - 48° - 72° = 60°

∠x and ∠ACD are on a straight line: ∠x = 180° - 60° = 120°

questions.label: Do and Learn (a)
questions.q: Find the unknown marked angle ∠a.
questions.hint: Start with 180° and take away the angles you know.
steps: The 3 angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
The angles we know are 105° and 48°.

questions.label: Do and Learn (b)
questions.q: Find the unknown marked angle ∠b.
questions.hint: Start with 180° and take away the angles you know.
steps: The 3 angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
The angles we know are 90° and 55°. The small square is a right angle, 90°.

questions.label: Do and Learn (c)
questions.q: Find the unknown marked angle ∠e.
questions.hint: All 3 sides have tick marks. What kind of triangle is it?
steps: All 3 sides have the same tick mark, so the triangle is equilateral.
An equilateral triangle has 3 equal angles. They add up to 180°.
questions.why: Every angle in an equilateral triangle is 60°.

questions.label: Do and Learn (d)
questions.q: Find the unknown marked angle ∠d.
questions.hint: Start with 180° and take away the angles you know.
steps: The 3 angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
The angles we know are 47° and 46°.

questions.label: Exercise 1 (a)
questions.q: Find the unknown marked angle ∠q.
questions.hint: Start with 180° and take away the angles you know.
steps: The 3 angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
The angles we know are 70° and 40°.

questions.label: Exercise 1 (b)
questions.q: Find the unknown marked angle ∠r.
questions.hint: Start with 180° and take away the angles you know.
steps: The 3 angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
The angles we know are 30° and 28°.

questions.label: Exercise 1 (c)
questions.q: Find the unknown marked angle ∠s.
questions.hint: Start with 180° and take away the angles you know.
steps: The 3 angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
The angles we know are 65° and 35°.

questions.label: Exercise 1 (d)
questions.q: Find the unknown marked angle ∠t.
questions.hint: Start with 180° and take away the angles you know.
steps: The 3 angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
The angles we know are 62° and 45°.

questions.label: Exercise 1 (e)
questions.q: Find the unknown marked angle ∠a.
questions.hint: Start with 180° and take away the angles you know.
steps: The 3 angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
The angles we know are 32° and 90°. The small square is a right angle, 90°.

questions.label: Exercise 1 (f)
questions.q: Find the unknown marked angle ∠b.
questions.hint: Start with 180° and take away the angles you know.
steps: The 3 angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
The angles we know are 78° and 58°.

questions.label: Exercise 2
questions.q: ACD is an equilateral triangle and BCD is a straight line. Find ∠b.
questions.hint: What is each angle of an equilateral triangle? What do angles on a straight line add up to?
steps: ACD is equilateral, so each of its angles is 60°. So ∠ACD = 60°.
BCD is a straight line. Angles on a straight line add up to 180°.
∠b and ∠ACD sit together on the straight line. So ∠b = 180° - 60°
questions.why: 60° + 120° = 180°, a straight line.

questions.label: Exercise 3
questions.q: PSR is a straight line and ∠PSQ and ∠PQR are right angles. Find ∠c and ∠d.
questions.hint: Look for right triangles. In a right triangle, the other 2 angles add up to 90°.
steps: Triangle QSR has a right angle at S (∠PSQ = 90°, so ∠QSR = 90° too).
Now look at the big triangle PQR. It has a right angle at Q.
So ∠d and ∠c add up to 90°. ∠d = 90° - 64° = 26°.
questions.why: Each right triangle's other 2 angles add up to 90°: 26° + 64° = 90° and 64° + 26° = 90°.

questions.label: Exercise 4
questions.q: EFH is an equilateral triangle. Find ∠g.
questions.hint: Look at the small triangle EGF. It has a right angle at G.
steps: EFH is equilateral, so ∠EFH = 60°.
Triangle EGF has a right angle at G. So ∠g and ∠EFG add up to 90°.
questions.why: In triangle EGF: 90° + 60° + 30° = 180°.

questions.label: Exercise 5
questions.q: KLM is a straight line. JLM is an isosceles triangle and JL = LM. Find ∠f.
questions.hint: JL = LM, so two angles of triangle JLM are equal. Then look at the big triangle JKM.
steps: In triangle JLM, JL = LM. The angles opposite these sides are equal, so ∠MJL = ∠JML = 30°.
Now look at the big triangle JMK. Its angles are 30° (at M), 90° (at K) and ∠MJK at J.
∠MJK = ∠MJL + ∠f = 30° + ∠f.

questions.label: Exercise 6
questions.q: PQR is a straight line and PS = RS. Find ∠e.
questions.hint: PS = RS, so ∠SPQ and ∠SRQ are equal. Then use the right triangle SQR.
steps: PS = RS, so triangle PSR is isosceles. The angles opposite the equal sides are equal: ∠SRQ = ∠SPQ = 25°.
Triangle SQR has a right angle at Q. So ∠e and ∠SRQ add up to 90°.
questions.why: In triangle SQR: 90° + 25° + 65° = 180°.

questions.label: Exercise 7
questions.q: ACD is an equilateral triangle. ABC is an isosceles triangle and AB = AC. Find ∠BCD.
questions.hint: ∠BCD is made of 2 parts: ∠ACD and ∠ACB. Find each part.
steps: ABC is isosceles with AB = AC, so ∠ACB = ∠ABC.
ACD is equilateral, so ∠ACD = 60°.
questions.why: ∠BCD is the 60° angle and the 72° angle put together.

questions.label: Exercise 8
questions.q: JKL and MKL are isosceles triangles and JK = JL and MK = ML. Find ∠JLM.
questions.hint: First find ∠JLK in the big triangle. Then take away ∠MLK.
steps: JK = JL, so ∠JLK = ∠JKL.
questions.why: ∠JLK (55°) is split into ∠JLM and ∠MLK (25°): 30° + 25° = 55°.

questions.label: Exercise 9
questions.q: STW is an equilateral triangle. SUV is an isosceles triangle. ∠VSW = ∠VSU = ∠UST. Find ∠SUV.
questions.hint: The 60° angle at S is cut into 3 equal parts.
steps: STW is equilateral, so ∠WST = 60°.
∠WST is cut into 3 equal angles. ∠VSU = 60° ÷ 3 = 20°
SUV is isosceles, so ∠SUV = ∠SVU.
questions.why: In triangle SUV: 20° + 80° + 80° = 180°.

questions.label: Exercise 10
questions.q: ABC is a right triangle such that ∠CAD = ½ ∠CAB. Find ∠DAB.
questions.hint: First find the whole angle ∠CAB. ∠CAD is half of it.
steps: Triangle ABC has a right angle at C and ∠ABC = 38°.
∠CAD is half of ∠CAB: ½ of 52° = 52° ÷ 2 = 26°
∠CAB is cut into 2 halves, so the other half is the same: ∠DAB = ∠CAD = 26°

learn.title: Drawing triangles on square grids
learn.html: Grid lines go straight across and straight up. So it is easy to make right angles and equal sides by counting squares.

learn.title: Right triangle and isosceles triangle on a grid
learn.html:
Triangle ABC: AC goes down 6 squares and CB goes across 6 squares. AC = BC and ∠ACB is a right angle.

Triangle DEF: D is right above the middle of EF. So DE = DF. It is isosceles.

learn.title: Your drawing tools
learn.html:
Ruler: draws straight lines and measures length in cm.

Protractor: measures and draws angles in degrees.

Set square: draws a right angle (90°).

Always draw a quick sketch first and write the measurements on it.

learn.title: Draw ABC: BC = 5 cm, ∠ABC = 50°, ∠ACB = 45°
learn.html:
Step 1: Draw a straight line BC 5 cm long.
Step 2: Put the protractor at B. Draw an angle of 50°.
Step 3: Put the protractor at C. Draw an angle of 45°.
Step 4: The 2 lines meet. Label this point A.

learn.title: Using a set square for a right angle
learn.html: Put one edge of the set square on the line. The other edge makes a line at 90°.

learn.title: Draw XYZ: XY = YZ = 5 cm, ∠XYZ = 90°
learn.html:
Step 1: Draw YZ 5 cm long.
Step 2: Use the set square to draw a line at Y that makes 90° with YZ.
Step 3: Measure 5 cm up from Y. Mark X.
Step 4: Join X and Z.

questions.label: Do and Learn
questions.q: Draw a triangle ABC in which BC = 6 cm, ∠ABC = 40° and ∠ACB = 55°.
questions.hint: Draw the side you know first (BC). Then draw the 2 angles at B and at C.
steps: Make a quick sketch. Write 6 cm on BC, 40° at B and 55° at C.
Use your ruler. Draw a straight line BC = 6 cm.
Put the centre of the protractor on B, with 0° on BC. Mark 40°. Draw a long line from B through the mark.
Put the centre of the protractor on C, with 0° on CB. Mark 55°. Draw a long line from C through the mark.
The 2 lines cross. Label this point A.
Check: ∠BAC should be 180° - 40° - 55° = 85°. Measure it with your protractor.
questions.why: The side and the 2 angles fix the triangle. The 3 angles add up to 180°.

questions.label: Exercise 1
questions.q: Draw a triangle ABC such that each side is equal to CB. (In your book, CB is 4 cm. Measure it with your ruler.)
questions.hint: If all 3 sides are equal, what type of triangle is it? What are its angles?
steps: Measure CB with your ruler. It is 4 cm.
Each side must be equal to CB, so AB = AC = CB = 4 cm. This is an equilateral triangle.
An equilateral triangle has 3 angles of 60°.
Draw CB 4 cm long. At C, draw an angle of 60° with the protractor. At B, draw an angle of 60°.
The 2 lines meet at A. Measure AB and AC. Each should be 4 cm.
questions.answer: An equilateral triangle ABC with each side 4 cm and each angle 60°
questions.why: All 3 sides are equal to CB, so the triangle is equilateral.

questions.label: Exercise 2
questions.q: Draw a triangle KLM in which ∠KLM = 70° and ∠LMK = 70°.
questions.hint: Draw the base ML first (any length). Then draw 70° at L and 70° at M.
steps: Sketch first: base ML, with 70° at L and 70° at M.
Draw a straight line ML. (Any length is fine, for example 6 cm.)
At L, use the protractor to draw an angle of 70°.
At M, use the protractor to draw an angle of 70°.
The 2 lines meet. Label the point K.
questions.why: 2 equal angles make an isosceles triangle (KL = KM). 70° + 70° + 40° = 180°.

questions.label: Exercise 3
questions.q: Draw a triangle EFG in which EF = 6 cm, GF = 5.5 cm and EG = 3.5 cm.
questions.hint: You know all 3 sides. Use a compass to find point G.
steps: Sketch first: EF = 6 cm, GF = 5.5 cm, EG = 3.5 cm.
Draw a straight line EF = 6 cm.
Open your compass to 3.5 cm. Put the needle on E and draw an arc above the line.
Open your compass to 5.5 cm. Put the needle on F and draw an arc that crosses the first arc.
The arcs cross at G. Join EG and FG with your ruler.
Check with your protractor: ∠E is about 65°, ∠G is about 80° and ∠F is about 35°. 65° + 80° + 35° = 180°.
questions.answer: Triangle EFG with EF = 6 cm, GF = 5.5 cm and EG = 3.5 cm (∠E ≈ 65°, ∠G ≈ 80°, ∠F ≈ 35°)
questions.why: G is 3.5 cm from E and 5.5 cm from F, so it is where the 2 arcs meet.

questions.label: Exercise 4
questions.q: Draw an equilateral triangle JKL such that each side is 5 cm long.
questions.hint: An equilateral triangle has three 60° angles.
steps: Sketch first: 3 sides of 5 cm and three angles of 60°.
Draw a straight line JK = 5 cm.
At J, draw an angle of 60°. At K, draw an angle of 60°.
The 2 lines meet at L.
Check: JL and KL should both measure 5 cm, and ∠L should be 60°.
questions.answer: Equilateral triangle JKL with each side 5 cm and each angle 60°
questions.why: 3 equal sides means 3 equal angles of 60°.

questions.label: Exercise 5
questions.q: Draw a right triangle XYZ such that XY = 6 cm, YZ = 3 cm and ∠XYZ = 90°.
questions.hint: Use a set square to make the right angle at Y.
steps: Sketch first: right angle at Y, XY = 6 cm, YZ = 3 cm.
Draw a straight line YZ = 3 cm.
Put the set square on YZ with the corner at Y. Draw a line at 90° to YZ.
Measure 6 cm along this line from Y. Mark X.
Join X and Z with your ruler.
questions.answer: Right triangle XYZ with XY = 6 cm, YZ = 3 cm and ∠XYZ = 90°
questions.why: The set square makes an exact right angle at Y.

questions.label: Exercise 6
questions.q: Draw an isosceles triangle PQR in which PQ = QR = 4 cm and ∠PQR = 135°.
questions.hint: Draw PQ first. The 135° angle is at Q, between the 2 equal sides.
steps: Sketch first: PQ = 4 cm, QR = 4 cm, ∠PQR = 135°.
Draw a straight line PQ = 4 cm.
Put the protractor at Q, with 0° on QP. Mark 135° and draw a line from Q.
Measure 4 cm along this line from Q. Mark R.
Join P and R.
Check: the other 2 angles are equal: (180° - 135°) ÷ 2 = 22.5° each.
questions.answer: Isosceles triangle PQR with PQ = QR = 4 cm and ∠PQR = 135°
questions.why: 2 equal sides with a 135° angle between them. It is isosceles and obtuse.

learn.title: Parts of a circle
learn.html:
Center (O): the point in the middle.

Radius (OD): a line from the center to the edge.

Diameter (AB): a line across the circle that goes through the center.

Chord (EF): any line joining 2 points on the edge.

Circumference: the distance all the way around.

learn.title: Is CD a diameter?
learn.html:
A diameter must go through the center O. If CD does not pass through O, it is only a chord.

The diameter is the longest chord of a circle.

Radii is the plural of radius: one radius, two radii.

learn.title: Radius and diameter
learn.html:
A diameter is 2 radii joined in a straight line.

Diameter = 2 × Radius

Radius = Diameter ÷ 2

learn.title: Radius 4 cm. Find the diameter.
learn.html:
Think of a pizza: from the middle to the edge is 4 cm. Across the whole pizza is 2 of those.

Diameter = 2 × 4 = 8 cm

learn.title: Diameter 15 m. Find the radius.
learn.html:
Radius = Diameter ÷ 2

= 15 ÷ 2 = 7.5 m

Or: Radius = ½ × 15 = 7.5 m

questions.label: Do and Learn 1 (a)
questions.q:
In the circle below, O is the center, AB and CD are the diameters.
AB = 18 cm
CD = ___ cm
questions.hint: Are all the diameters of one circle the same length?
steps: AB and CD both go through the center O, so both are diameters.
All the diameters of the same circle are the same length.
So CD = AB = 18 cm.
questions.why: Every diameter of a circle has the same length.

questions.label: Do and Learn 1 (b)
questions.q:
In the circle below, O is the center, OA and OB are the radii.
OA = 7 cm
OB = ___ cm
questions.hint: Are all the radii of one circle the same length?
steps: OA and OB both go from the center O to the edge, so both are radii.
All the radii of the same circle are the same length.
So OB = OA = 7 cm.
questions.why: Every radius of a circle has the same length.

questions.label: Do and Learn 2 (a)
questions.q:
O is the center. Find the diameter of the circle.
Diameter = ___ cm
questions.hint: The 6 cm line goes from the center to the edge. Is it a radius or a diameter?
steps: The 6 cm line goes from O to the edge, so the radius is 6 cm.
Diameter = 2 × Radius
questions.why: A diameter is 2 radii: 6 cm + 6 cm = 12 cm.

questions.label: Do and Learn 2 (b)
questions.q:
O is the center. Find the radius of the circle.
Radius = ___ cm
questions.hint: The 24 cm line goes right across through O. Is it a radius or a diameter?
steps: The 24 cm line goes across the circle through O, so the diameter is 24 cm.
Radius = Diameter ÷ 2
questions.why: The radius is half of the diameter: 12 + 12 = 24.

questions.label: Do and Learn 3
questions.q:
What are the missing values in the table?
CircleRadiusDiameter
W13 cm?
X?13 cm
Y?38 cm
Z22 cm?
questions.hint: Radius to diameter: × 2. Diameter to radius: ÷ 2.
steps: W: Diameter = 2 × 13 = 26 cm
X: Radius = 13 ÷ 2 = 6½ cm (half of 12 is 6, half of 1 is ½)
Y: Radius = 38 ÷ 2 = 19 cm
Z: Diameter = 2 × 22 = 44 cm
questions.answer: W: 26 cm, X: 6½ cm, Y: 19 cm, Z: 44 cm
questions.why: The diameter is always 2 times the radius.

questions.label: Exercise 1
questions.q:
Use the words given to name the parts of a circle.
circumference · center · radius · diameter · chord
questions.hint: A line through the center is special. A line from the center to the edge is special too.
steps: Label 1 points to the line all the way around the circle: circumference.
Label 2 points to the line across the circle through the center: diameter (it is also a chord).
Label 3 points to a line joining 2 points on the edge, not through the center: chord.
Label 4 points to the line from the center to the edge: radius.
Label 5 points to the middle point: center.
questions.why: A diameter goes through the center, a radius starts at the center, and a chord joins any 2 points on the edge.

questions.label: Exercise 2 (a)
questions.q:
Fill in the blanks.
Center: ___
Diameter: ___
Radius: ___
Chord: ___ and ___
questions.hint: Find the dot in the middle first. Then check which lines go through it.
steps: The dot in the middle is O. That is the center.
AB goes across the circle through O. So the diameter is AB.
CO goes from the edge to the center. So the radius is CO.
A chord joins 2 points on the edge: EF and AB (a diameter is also a chord).
questions.answer: Center: O; Diameter: AB; Radius: CO; Chord: EF and AB
questions.why: AB passes through O, so it is a diameter and also the longest chord.

questions.label: Exercise 2 (b)
questions.q:
Fill in the blanks.
Center: ___
Diameter: ___
Radius: ___
Chord: ___ and ___
questions.hint: Which line goes through O from one side to the other?
steps: The dot in the middle is O. That is the center.
TU goes across the circle through O. So the diameter is TU.
SO goes from the edge to the center. So the radius is SO.
The chords join 2 points on the edge: TP and TU.
questions.answer: Center: O; Diameter: TU; Radius: SO; Chord: TP and TU
questions.why: TU passes through O, so it is a diameter and also a chord.

questions.label: Exercise 2 (c)
questions.q:
Fill in the blanks.
Center: ___
Diameter: ___
Radius: ___
Chord: ___ and ___
questions.hint: Careful! The center here is not called O. Find the dot in the middle.
steps: The dot in the middle is A. That is the center.
KM goes across the circle through A. So the diameter is KM.
PA goes from the edge to the center. So the radius is PA.
The chords join 2 points on the edge: KN and KM. (U is only where 2 lines cross, not on the edge.)
questions.answer: Center: A; Diameter: KM; Radius: PA; Chord: KN and KM
questions.why: KM passes through the center A, so it is a diameter and also a chord.

questions.label: Exercise 3
questions.q:
Fill in the blanks.
(a) ___ : The straight line joining any two points on the circumference of a circle
(b) ___ : The straight line joining the center and the circumference of a circle
(c) ___ : The distance around a circle
(d) ___ : The straight line that passes through the center of a circle
(e) ___ : The point in the middle of a circle
questions.hint: Use the words: chord, radius, circumference, diameter, center.
steps: (a) Any 2 points on the edge: Chord
(b) From the center to the edge: Radius
(c) All the way around: Circumference
(d) Through the center: Diameter
(e) The middle point: Center
questions.why: Each part of a circle has its own name.

questions.label: Exercise 4
questions.q:
Draw the given parts of a circle. (Answers vary.)
Center: A
Diameter: BC
Radius: AD
Chord: CE and BF
questions.hint: Mark the center A first. A diameter must pass through A.
steps: Draw a circle. Mark the center and call it A.
Draw a line across the circle through A. Call the ends B and C. That is the diameter BC.
Draw a line from A to the edge. Call the end D. That is the radius AD.
Mark points E and F on the edge. Join C to E and B to F. These are the chords CE and BF.
questions.answer: One possible drawing is shown (answers vary)
questions.why: Any drawing is correct if BC goes through A, AD starts at A, and CE and BF join 2 points on the edge.

questions.label: Exercise 5 (a)
questions.q:
Find the radius of the circle.
O is the center and AB is the diameter of the circle. AB = 12 cm.
Radius = ___ cm
questions.hint: AB is a diameter. Halve it.
steps: The diameter is 12 cm.
Radius = Diameter ÷ 2
questions.why: 6 + 6 = 12, the diameter.

questions.label: Exercise 5 (b)
questions.q:
Find the radius of the circle.
O is the center and CD is the diameter of the circle. CD = 25 cm.
Radius = ___ cm
questions.hint: CD is a diameter. Halve it.
steps: The diameter is 25 cm.
Radius = Diameter ÷ 2
questions.why: 12.5 + 12.5 = 25, the diameter.

questions.label: Exercise 5 (c)
questions.q:
Find the radius of the circle. The circle fits exactly inside a square of side 18 cm.
Radius = ___ cm
questions.hint: The circle touches all 4 sides of the square. How wide is the circle?
steps: The circle fits exactly inside the square, so the circle is as wide as the square.
So the diameter is 18 cm.
Radius = 18 ÷ 2 = 9 cm
questions.why: The width of the square is the diameter of the circle.

questions.label: Exercise 5 (d)
questions.q:
Find the radius of the circle. ABCD is a square in a circle. BD = 30 cm.
Radius = ___ cm
questions.hint: BD goes from one corner of the square to the opposite corner. Does it go through the center of the circle?
steps: The corners of the square are on the circle. BD joins opposite corners, so it goes through the center.
So BD is a diameter: 30 cm.
Radius = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm
questions.why: The diagonal of the square passes through the center, so it is a diameter.

questions.label: Exercise 6
questions.q:
O is the center of the circle. What are the lengths of OB and CD?
OA = 32 cm
OB = ___ cm
CD = ___ cm
questions.hint: OA and OB are both radii. CD goes through O.
steps: OA goes from the center to the edge, so the radius is 32 cm.
OB is also a radius. So OB = 32 cm.
CD goes across through O, so it is a diameter.
questions.why: All radii are equal, and a diameter is 2 radii.

questions.label: Exercise 7
questions.q:
What are the lengths of the diameter and radius of the wheel?
h = 60 cm
diameter = ___ cm
radius = ___ cm
questions.hint: h is the height of the wheel from the very bottom to the very top.
steps: h goes from the bottom of the wheel to the top, straight through the middle. That is the diameter.
So the diameter = 60 cm.
Radius = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 cm
questions.why: The height of a wheel is the same as its diameter.

questions.label: Exercise 8 (a)
questions.q:
Find the diameter of the circle.
OH is the radius of the circle. OH = 10 cm.
Diameter = ___ cm
questions.hint: Diameter = 2 × Radius
steps: The radius is 10 cm.
Diameter = 2 × Radius

questions.label: Exercise 8 (b)
questions.q:
Find the diameter of the circle.
OR is the radius of the circle. OR = 14.5 cm.
Diameter = ___ cm
questions.hint: Diameter = 2 × Radius
steps: The radius is 14.5 cm.
Diameter = 2 × Radius

questions.label: Exercise 8 (c)
questions.q:

O is the center of the circle. The radius is 12 cm.
Diameter = ___ cm
questions.hint: Diameter = 2 × Radius
steps: The radius is 12 cm.
Diameter = 2 × Radius

questions.label: Exercise 8 (d)
questions.q:
Find the diameter of the circle. PQRS is a square in a circle. The 2 halves of the diagonal measure 3.5 cm each.
Diameter = ___ cm
questions.hint: The corners of the square sit on the circle. A diagonal goes through the center.
steps: The diagonal PR of the square goes through the center O, so it is a diameter.
Each half of the diagonal is a radius: 3.5 cm.
Diameter = 3.5 + 3.5 = 7 cm
questions.why: The diagonal of the square is a diameter of the circle.

learn.title: Using a compass
learn.html:
A compass has a needle and a pencil. The gap between them is the radius of the circle.

Use a ruler to set the gap.

learn.title: Draw a circle with radius 1 cm
learn.html:
Step 1: Mark O as the center.
Step 2: Open the compass to 1 cm using a ruler.
Step 3: Put the needle on O and the pencil on the paper. Turn the compass.
Step 4: Keep turning until the circle is complete.

learn.title: Given the diameter? Find the radius first!
learn.html:
A compass is set to the radius, not the diameter.

Radius = Diameter ÷ 2

learn.title: Draw a circle with diameter 4 cm
learn.html:
Radius = 4 ÷ 2 = 2 cm.

Mark O. Open the compass to 2 cm. Put the needle on O and turn the compass all the way round.

Make sure the circle joins up completely.

learn.title: A string and a pin
learn.html:
Tie a string to a pin and a pencil. Hold the pin still and pull the string tight. Go round the pin with the pencil.

The length of the string is the radius. (Be careful: pins are sharp!)

questions.label: Do and Learn
questions.q: Draw a circle O in which its radius is 3 cm long.
questions.hint: The compass gap is the radius.
steps: Mark a point and call it O. This is the center.
Use a ruler to open the compass to 3 cm.
Put the needle on O. Turn the compass all the way round to draw the circle.
questions.answer: A circle with center O and radius 3 cm
questions.why: Every point on the circle is 3 cm from O.

questions.label: Exercise 1
questions.q: Draw a circle A in which its radius is 2.5 cm long.
questions.hint: Open the compass to the radius.
steps: Mark a point and call it A. This is the center.
Use a ruler to open the compass to 2.5 cm (2 and a half cm).
Put the needle on A. Turn the compass all the way round.
questions.answer: A circle with center A and radius 2.5 cm
questions.why: The compass gap is the radius, 2.5 cm.

questions.label: Exercise 2
questions.q: Draw a circle B in which its diameter is 7 cm long.
questions.hint: You are given the diameter. Find the radius first.
steps: Find the radius: 7 ÷ 2 = 3.5 cm.
Mark the center B.
Open the compass to 3.5 cm. Put the needle on B and draw the circle.
Check: measure across the circle through B. It should be 7 cm.
questions.answer: A circle with center B and radius 3.5 cm (diameter 7 cm)
questions.why: Radius = 7 ÷ 2 = 3.5 cm.

questions.label: Exercise 3
questions.q: Draw a circle E in which its radius is equal to AB. (Measure AB in your book. It is 4 cm.)
questions.hint: Measure AB first. That length is the radius.
steps: Measure AB with your ruler. AB = 4 cm.
The radius must be equal to AB, so the radius is 4 cm.
Mark the center E. Open the compass to 4 cm and draw the circle.
questions.answer: A circle with center E and radius 4 cm
questions.why: The radius is the same length as AB.

questions.label: Exercise 4
questions.q: Draw a circle F in which its diameter is equal to GD. (Measure GD in your book. It is 6 cm.)
questions.hint: GD is the diameter. The compass needs the radius.
steps: Measure GD with your ruler. GD = 6 cm. This is the diameter.
Radius = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm.
Mark the center F. Open the compass to 3 cm and draw the circle.
questions.answer: A circle with center F and radius 3 cm (diameter 6 cm)
questions.why: The diameter is GD = 6 cm, so the radius is 3 cm.

questions.label: Exercise 5
questions.q: Create a straight line AB of 8 cm long. Then draw a circle in which its center is E and its diameter is AB.
questions.hint: The center of a diameter is exactly in the middle of it.
steps: Draw a straight line AB = 8 cm.
AB is the diameter, so the center is in the middle. Measure 4 cm from A and mark E.
Radius = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm.
Open the compass to 4 cm. Put the needle on E and draw the circle. It passes through A and B.
questions.answer: A circle with center E (the middle of AB) and radius 4 cm
questions.why: E is the middle of the diameter AB, so EA = EB = 4 cm.

questions.label: Exercise 6
questions.q: Draw a square in which its diagonals are 4 cm long. With O as the center, draw a circle such that its circumference meets all four vertices of the square.
questions.hint: The diagonals of a square cross in the middle at right angles. Each half is 2 cm.
steps: Draw 2 lines of 4 cm that cross in the middle at right angles. Mark the middle point O.
Join the 4 ends. This is the square.
From O to each corner is half a diagonal: 4 ÷ 2 = 2 cm. This is the radius.
Open the compass to 2 cm. Put the needle on O and draw the circle. It passes through all 4 corners.
questions.answer: A circle with center O and radius 2 cm passing through the 4 corners of the square
questions.why: Each corner is 2 cm from O, so a circle of radius 2 cm touches all 4 corners.

learn.title: Unit 7 big ideas
learn.html:
Sides: equilateral (3 equal), isosceles (2 equal), scalene (none equal).

Angles: acute (all less than 90°), right (one 90°), obtuse (one more than 90°).

learn.title: Angle facts
learn.html:
The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. Angles on a straight line add up to 180°.

In a right triangle, the other 2 angles add up to 90°.

learn.title: Circle facts
learn.html: Diameter = 2 × Radius and Radius = Diameter ÷ 2. Set the compass to the radius.

learn.title: Problem solving plan
learn.html:
Understand: What is given? What must I find?
Plan: Which facts can I use?
Solve: Work step by step.
Check: Do the angles add up to 180°?

questions.label: Let's Think Along
questions.q: The figure shows 2 triangles. ABC is an isosceles triangle and DBC is an equilateral triangle. Find ∠ACD.
questions.hint: ∠ACD = ∠ACB - ∠DCB. Find both angles.
steps: ABC is isosceles, so ∠ACB = ∠ABC.
DBC is equilateral, so ∠DCB = 60°.
questions.why: ∠ACB (70°) is made of ∠ACD and ∠DCB (60°): 10° + 60° = 70°.

questions.label: Problem Solving
questions.q: In the figure below, ABC and AED are straight lines and BE = ED. Find ∠ABE.
questions.hint: BE = ED, so triangle BED is isosceles. Use the angle sum of the big triangle ACD.
steps: Understand: We know ∠A = 36°, ∠C = 64° and ∠EBD = 38°. We must find ∠ABE.
BE = ED, so the angles opposite them are equal: ∠BDE = ∠EBD = 38°.
In the big triangle ACD: ∠ADC = 180° - 36° - 64° = 80°. So ∠BDC = 80° - 38° = 42°.
In triangle BCD: ∠CBD = 180° - 64° - 42° = 74°.
ABC is a straight line (180°): ∠ABE = 180° - 38° - 74° = 68°.
questions.why: The angles on the straight line ABC add up to 180°: 68° + 38° + 74° = 180°.

questions.label: Math Journal
questions.q:
Siti: Can I draw a triangle that has 1 obtuse angle and 2 acute angles?
Janice: Can I draw a triangle that has 1 obtuse angle and 1 right angle?
Peter: Can I draw a triangle that has 2 right angles?
Which child will be able to draw his or her triangle? Draw figures to help you explain the reasons.
questions.hint: The 3 angles must add up to exactly 180°. Try some numbers.
steps: Siti: try 120°, 30° and 30°. 120° + 30° + 30° = 180° ✓. So Siti can draw it.
Janice: an obtuse angle is more than 90°. Add a right angle: more than 90° + 90° = more than 180°. That is too much. Janice cannot.
Peter: 90° + 90° = 180° already. The third angle would be 0°. Peter cannot.
In a right triangle, the other 2 angles add up to 90°, so they must both be acute.
questions.answer: Only Siti can draw her triangle.
questions.why: The angle sum of a triangle is 180°. Janice's and Peter's triangles would need more than 180°.
